claims.text: At stage-3 DonHang.Notifications registers OrderEventsConsumer with AddHostedService (Program.cs:26) beside NotificationSender (line 31); OrderEventsConsumer derives from BackgroundService and consumes notifications.order-events.
HandleAsync reads the message and adds one notifications row with Status = "pending" (plus an inbox_messages row) and calls SaveChangesAsync; NotificationSender sends pending rows as emails.
OrderEventsConsumer is a driving adapter: like OrdersController with an HTTP request, it turns a message from outside into a call to the service's own code.

With manual acknowledgement (autoAck: false), RabbitMQ keeps a delivered message as unacknowledged and does not deliver it to other consumers until the consumer answers it (ack, reject or nack) or its channel/connection closes; on close it is requeued and delivered again.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms > Delivery Acknowledgement Modes; Automatic Requeueing

claims.text: With automatic acknowledgement, RabbitMQ considers a message delivered (and removes it) as soon as it is sent to the consumer.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Consumer Acknowledgements and Publisher Confirms > Acknowledgement Modes (automatic, 'fire-and-forget')

claims.text: BasicConsumeAsync(queue, autoAck: false, consumer) subscribes with manual acknowledgement; BasicAckAsync(deliveryTag, multiple: false) acknowledges only the delivery with that tag; acks are sent on the channel the delivery came on.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ .NET client 7.x API guide: Consuming / Acknowledging; RabbitMQ docs: Confirms > Channels and Delivery Tags; OrderEventsConsumer.cs:55,75

claims.text: OnReceivedAsync calls BasicAckAsync (line 75) only after HandleAsync (line 74) returns; it is the method's only ack. Lines 77-86 reject (requeue: false) a PoisonMessageException and nack with requeue: true any other exception.

Line 49 opens the channel with await using; line 50 declares queue and binding; line 51 sets prefetch (BasicQosAsync); line 54 attaches OnReceivedAsync. Line 56 waits until stoppingToken is cancelled; leaving the method disposes the channel, which closes it.

claims.text: Acknowledging after the save makes consuming at-least-once: a crash before the save requeues the message (nothing lost); a crash after the save and before the ack delivers it again. Acknowledging before the save makes it at-most-once.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Consumer Acknowledgements > Delivery Acknowledgement Timeout / Automatic Requeueing; Reliability Guide > Consumers; prereq backend.l2.at-least-once-jobs

claims.text: When several consumers consume one queue, RabbitMQ normally hands each delivery to one of them in round-robin; a requeued message may go to a different consumer; a service gets every message only through a queue of its own bound to the exchange.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Consumers (multiple consumers on a queue, round-robin); Tutorial 2 Work Queues; OrderEventsConsumer.cs:14-15 (comment)

claims.text: RabbitMQ reports per queue the number of messages ready for delivery and the number unacknowledged; unacknowledged messages become ready again when their channel closes.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs: Monitoring > per-queue metrics (messages_ready, messages_unacknowledged); Confirms > Automatic Requeueing
